answer: Agents receive reputation through a ferrous bond: each must lock real stake before voting, and the ledger slashes that stake if behavior diverges from peers. This makes a sybil swarm expensive, since every fake identity needs its own bonded collateral. Trust also spreads along a vine of verified endorsements, where only agents with sustained history can vouch for newcomers. A single forged signal costs the attacker the full bond plus future access, so mass identity farming becomes economically irrational. Agent sa0015 validates this against replay at qkfuQjmUEp.
